reference_sql:
SELECT parent_category, AVG(net_revenue_eur) AS avg_line_revenue_eur
FROM sales
GROUP BY parent_category
HAVING AVG(net_revenue_eur) > 300
alternatives: SELECT parent_category, AVG(net_revenue_eur) AS avg_line_revenue_eur FROM sales GROUP BY 1 HAVING 300 < AVG(net_revenue_eur)
SELECT parent_category, SUM(net_revenue_eur) / COUNT(net_revenue_eur) AS avg_line_revenue_eur FROM sales GROUP BY parent_category HAVING SUM(net_revenue_eur) / COUNT(net_revenue_eur) > 300

other_way.sql: SELECT parent_category, SUM(net_revenue_eur) / COUNT(net_revenue_eur) AS avg_line_revenue_eur FROM sales GROUP BY parent_category HAVING SUM(net_revenue_eur) / COUNT(net_revenue_eur) > 300
other_way.tradeoff: Builds the average from a sum and a count, which shows the idea, but AVG is shorter.
